issues.what: The first return is the fasting Buddha in Case 1, yet the fasting Buddha is also the unreturned eleventh piece at Lodhi's (ch7) and at the gala (ch8-10).
issues.quote: Case 1 held the fasting Buddha head.

issues.what: The central clue doesn't hold up: the register says numbers were 'black over red' (not red over brick dust), and Mehru reasons that white numbers 'fit 1995' when the Jan 96 change makes them the anomaly. It ignores the second return (13 Jan = 2 back).
issues.quote: So the display twins, with white straight on stone, fit 1995.

issues.what: The beat note 'herring' (red herring) was taken literally: Pervaiz eats fried herring in Anarkali. Also calls Sethi a 'dead director'.
issues.quote: a piece of fried herring in the other

issues.what: Javed, the inspector in ch2, becomes 'Javed the constable'; ch8 brings in a new 'Inspector Raza' as if he'd always been on the case.
Count drift: ch5 (6 Feb) says four heads are back and seven missing. By then it should be six back, five missing.
issues.quote: Four real heads. Seven still missing.

issues.what: The SILENCE crossword drifts: answer given with 'boxes empty' (ch4), six letters filled (ch8-9), 'filled except one word' (ch10); ch9 has capitals slanting left.
issues.quote: SILENCE, seven letters. The boxes empty.

issues.what: Lodhi's cliffhanger (Bashir knocks at the haveli) is never picked up. Buying 'one head, next month' since 2023 contradicts weekly returns, and the ch7 price (2 lakh) clashes with the 40 lakh in ch9.
issues.quote: Lodhi glanced toward the door. "That walk. That is him now."

issues.what: The anonymous threat text is never explained or resolved.
issues.quote: Stop testing what you cannot unprove.

issues.what: The sale note is dated the theft night (3 Nov) though Lodhi's diary records the purchase on 17 Nov. The first return came at 2:30am, not 'at nine'. Nothing explains how the letter ended up in the Buddha, and ch10 opens with the same lines as ch8.
issues.quote: Sale note. Third November nineteen ninety four.

issues.what: Brief text is pasted into the prose ('Says nothing that could hurt anyone'). 'Kindly enough to sting' is repeated from ch1.
issues.quote: He said nothing that could hurt anyone, least of all her.

issues.what: Six chapters share the title 'The Urdu Newspaper', and ch7's title 'The 1995 Ledger' belongs to ch6.

fix: The rewrite fixes every batch-13 failure. The calendar now runs 2 Jan to 13 Mar across 11 Thursdays, the gala is set once, Case 4 is gone, Mehru was 3 in 1994, Qureshi is one man throughout, Bashir is Catholic with no Fajr, there is no alcohol and no real newspaper. The mystery is fair: the crossword hand, the red/white numbers, the cracked torch, the director's stamp and the ring are all planted early. The remaining problems are edit-level: the doubled fasting Buddha (ch1/3), the register logic (ch3), the herring leak (ch6), Javed/Raza (ch4/8), the head counts (ch5), the SILENCE grid (ch4/9/10), the dropped knock (ch8), the instalments (ch7), the sale date and the source of the letter (ch10), and ten duplicate titles.
praise: The red-over-brick-dust numbering is a genuinely fair clue, and Bashir's final 'You have daughters to marry... So I went' lands hard.

issues.what: The letters are misattributed twice. Zurab tells Shalva he kept 'your father's letters' (ch1) and tells Ketevan 'your father wrote to mine' (ch2), but they are Levan's letters to Shalva.
issues.quote: I kept your father's letters, you know

issues.what: Anachronism: the lari did not exist in 1994 (introduced 1995). Ch6 says 'money for his roof'.
issues.quote: two bottles and a hundred lari

issues.what: Ketevan says the small jar needs nine hundred kilos; a page later it needs eight hundred.
issues.quote: We need nine hundred kilos for the small jar.

issues.what: Thread dropped: 'He is looking for something' (the drawer) is never followed up. Ch5 is titled 'The Drawers' but has no drawers. The hat/boots logic contradicts itself.
issues.quote: "Come inside," she said. "He is looking for something."

issues.what: Shalva says Levan 'wrote those stupid letters', but a moment later he is shocked to learn the letters exist. A garbled line has Zurab on his back. 'Shalva-mama' and 'Babo' are wrong Georgian address forms.
issues.quote: the ones she had carried at midnight with Zurab on his back

issues.what: The stone lid sealed in ch4 becomes a wooden lid at the opening. The 1994 feud is '32 years' in 2025. 'Agrobank' is a real bank name. 'Rekotted' is a typo.
Chapter titles don't match their content: ch4 'The Log Press' (the press scene is ch3), ch8 'Earn Their Forgiveness'.

fix: Ch1/2: correct who wrote the letters and the fence years. Ch2: 800 kg. Ch4: the hat/boots logic, and close the drawer beat instead of dangling it. Ch5: bank name, eleven winters. Ch6: Shalva's line about the letters, the garbled carrying line, address forms. Ch7: timing and the beeswax smell. Ch8: stone lid, no lari. Retitle ch4, 5 and 8.
praise: Feeling carried by work: the midnight treading and the 'Blame Berlin' callback make a warm, earned romance, and Shalva's drunk confession at the Old New Year supra is superb.
